Lecture recorder app: record, transcribe and summarize your classes

Verbi Lecture Recorder & Notes is a lecture recorder app for iPhone and Android. Record the whole class on your phone, or import a recording you already have, and Verbi writes the full transcript in any of 39 languages, then turns it into lesson notes that stick to what the lecturer said. It’s free to start, with 60 minutes of transcription every month.

Free to download, with 60 minutes of transcription every month.

Last updated: November 1, 2026

What does the Verbi lecture recorder app do?

  • Records the whole class. Verbi has no maximum recording length, and on iPhone it keeps recording with the screen locked.
  • Imports a lecture you already have: an audio or video file, a recording shared from another app, or a YouTube link.
  • Transcribes it from the first minute to the last, in any of 39 languages, with automatic language detection.
  • Turns the transcript into lesson notes with the Lesson Notes template, keeping to what was taught.
  • Finds any lecture by anything that was said in it. With Pro, you can also ask a lecture questions, translate it and export it.

How do I record and transcribe a college lecture?

  1. Make sure recording is allowed in the course. If you’re not sure, ask the lecturer.
  2. Before class, add course terms, names and acronyms to Custom Vocabulary in Settings, so they come out spelled right.
  3. When the lecture starts, tap Record & Transcribe and put the phone where it can hear the lecturer clearly. Choose Live Transcription instead if you want to read along as they speak.
  4. On iPhone, you can lock the screen and the recording continues. On Android, keep Verbi open on the recording screen, with the screen on, until you tap Stop.
  5. Tap Stop when the class ends, and Verbi transcribes the recording. On Android, and on iPhone with iOS 26 or later, a long lecture keeps transcribing if you leave the app, and Verbi tells you when your notes are ready; on older iOS versions, the upload continues in the background and the transcription is ready when you reopen Verbi.

Can I transcribe a lecture I already recorded?

  1. Open Verbi, tap Upload File and pick the recording. Audio files such as M4A, MP3 and WAV work, and so do video files: Verbi transcribes their sound.
  2. Or share the recording to Verbi from the app it’s in, such as Voice Memos or Files. On iPhone, open Verbi afterwards to start the transcript.
  3. If the lecture is on YouTube, tap Load from YouTube and paste the link; the YouTube video to text guide has the steps.
  4. Verbi transcribes an imported lecture like one recorded in the app. It counts toward your plan’s hours, or on the free plan toward the same 60 minutes a month. More in importing an audio file.

How do I get lecture notes from an audio recording?

  1. Open the recording and go to its Summary tab.
  2. With Pro, tap the template button, choose Lesson Notes and tap Generate Summary. Pro also writes a summary on its own after every transcript, with your default template.
  3. On the free plan, your first transcript gets one AI summary automatically.
  4. With Pro, ask the lecture what you missed, such as “What did she say about the exam?”, and export your notes as PDF or TXT. On the free plan, copy the text.

What do the transcript and the lesson notes include?

  • The whole lecture as text, from the first minute to the last, with timestamps.
  • Lesson notes that follow the structure of the class: definitions, rules, formulas, worked examples and the lecturer’s explanations, kept as they were said.
  • Homework, readings and exam dates, listed only when the lecturer mentioned them. Verbi doesn’t add textbook material that wasn’t part of the class.
  • Unclear terms marked as unclear instead of guessed.
  • Search across all your recordings, and with Pro a chat with any lecture.
  • Lectures in 39 languages, with translation into English, Turkish, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Russian, Arabic, Japanese, Korean, Indonesian, Dutch, Polish or Simplified Chinese on Pro.

How do I record a lecture clearly?

  • Sit near the front, or close to a loudspeaker if the lecturer uses a microphone. Distance costs more clarity than anything else.
  • Lay the phone flat on the desk, away from your laptop keyboard, so typing doesn’t drown out the voice.
  • On iPhone, a phone call pauses the recording and keeps what came before it. If it doesn’t continue on its own afterwards, tap Resume.
  • On the free plan, recordings are kept for 15 days: copy the text you want to keep, or go Pro to export TXT or PDF and keep everything.

Can I record lectures on the free plan?

Yes. The free plan includes 60 minutes of transcription a month, live transcription (basic on iPhone), recordings kept for 15 days and only your first AI summary. That’s enough to try Verbi in one class, though a lecture longer than an hour uses up the month’s free minutes on its own, and on iPhone the recording stops when they run out.

For a full term, with lesson notes after every class, Verbi Pro gives you hours of transcription (20 a month, or 5 a week on the weekly plan; MAX doubles that), an AI summary for every transcript, speaker detection, translation, chat with the transcript, export, high-quality live transcription on iPhone and recordings kept past 15 days. The app shows the price in your currency before you subscribe.

Recordings and transcripts are stored on your phone; Verbi has no account and no cloud sync. The privacy policy explains what is sent for transcription and summaries.

Frequently asked questions

What is Verbi Lecture Recorder & Notes?

It’s the name of Verbi on the App Store: the voice recorder and note taker from theverbi.com. The same app is on Google Play for Android. It records lectures, meetings and interviews, transcribes them and turns them into notes.

Can Verbi record a 90-minute lecture?

Yes, with Verbi Pro: a 90-minute lecture is well within its 20 hours a month (5 a week on the weekly plan). The free plan includes 60 minutes of transcription a month, so a lecture that long needs Pro; on iPhone, a free recording stops when the minutes run out.

Can I transcribe a lecture I recorded with another app?

Yes. Tap Upload File in Verbi, or share the recording to Verbi from the app it’s in. It’s transcribed like a recording made in Verbi, and on the free plan it counts toward the 60 minutes a month.

Will the notes include things the lecturer didn’t say?

No. Lesson notes stick to the recording: Verbi doesn’t add textbook knowledge, examples or formulas that weren’t part of the class, and it marks a term as unclear rather than guessing.

Can I record lectures in another language?

Yes. Verbi transcribes 39 languages, and with Pro you can translate the transcript into English, Turkish, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Russian, Arabic, Japanese, Korean, Indonesian, Dutch, Polish or Simplified Chinese.

Where are my lecture recordings stored?

On your phone: Verbi has no account and no cloud sync. To transcribe, the audio is sent to our speech-to-text providers, usually through our server, and summaries, chat and translation send the transcript text to our AI provider. The privacy policy lists what is sent and where.
